newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lawmakers ask Clinton to push for Vanunu release.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lawmakers ask Clinton to push for Vanunu release.

text.p: A group of House of Representatives Democrats on Thursday asked U.S. President Bill Clinton to push for the release of Mordechai Vanunu, a former nuclear technician convicted of spying against Israel.
In a letter to the president, 13 lawmakers said Vanunu, who has been held in solitary confinement in Israel for more than a decade, should be freed for humanitarian reasons.
Vanunu was convicted of treason against Israel for revealing that government officials had built up a stockpile of nuclear weapons.

"We do not mean to imply endorsement of his actions, but we believe he has suffered enough for what he sincerely believed to be an act of conscience," said the lawmakers, led by California Democratic Representative Ron Dellums.
"While having no desire to interfere in the internal affairs of a foreign state, we believe that the Vanunu case has human rights implications transcending national boundaries," it said.
The lawmakers said there were indications that Vanunu was under increasing mental stress.
Vanunu provided pictures to newspapers in 1986 to help prove Israel controlled a nuclear arsenal. His case has been taken up by international human rights organisations.
Israeli President Weizman on a visit to Britain last month dismissed any suggestion of a pardon, calling Vanunu a traitor.
